result:
Done. All six deliverables worked in order, everything run in the foreground.

## What I reproduced (D1, before any change)

Own pier: `~/piers/joinall-bus` (fake `~bus`), HTTP 8093, Vere 4.6, stock git 2.55.0. Running source confirmed by scry at every step, never by reading the mount.

- **Defect 1** — two refs in one push → `HTTP/1.1 400 missing`. The same two refs pushed one at a time both returned exit 0.
- **Defect 2** — 11 MB single-ref push with default `http.postBuffer` → git sent `Content-Length: 4` (the `0000` probe), got 400, aborted before offering the pack.

## What I changed

Two commits on `feat/progress-and-joinall`, plus the report. Not pushed.

- `7c86699` — `parse-receive-command` accepts end-of-payload as a ref terminator alongside NUL and LF. Same rule for every line; `valid-ref` unchanged.
- `f70e6a8` — new `receive-probe` arm; `handle-receive-pack` answers a flush-only body with 200 + empty `x-git-receive-pack-result` body, after auth and before parsing. `parse-receive-request` untouched.
- `455bcb6` — `PUSH-DEFECTS.md`.

I installed fix 1 **alone** first and confirmed on the pier that it fixes defect 1 and leaves defect 2 failing, so each commit is verified in isolation.

## D3 evidence

- **One command, 5 branches + 2 tags (one annotated), no `-c` flags at all** → all 7 refs created, 11,451,409-byte body, wall 1.37–1.43 s. Literal `git push --all` (5 branches) and `git push --tags` also pass; they cannot be combined on one command line, which is why the refspec form is the headline test.
- **Clone back** (v0 and v2, `--mirror`): `git rev-list --objects --all | sort | sha256sum` = `21db089d…4d170b8`, **identical to source**, 1,373 objects each. `git fsck --full` exit 0, no output, both clones.
- **All 18 vectors** built and ran; the four named ones pass with their products read out (`git-codec-vector` gives `3b18e512dba79e4c8300dd08aeb37f8e728b8dad`). One correction: `JOIN-ALL-PERFORMANCE.md` §4b has the right values but rotates the labels across `git-pack-decode-vector` / `git-pack-vector` / `git-shallow-vector`. Nothing regressed — `pack-decode` returns the same noun as `inflate` and `zlib`, so it must share their mug.
- Negative tests: `0000GARBAGE`, garbage, empty body, and a bad ref name all still 400; an unauthenticated probe still 401.

## Verdict on the `protocol.version=2` 400

**Defect 2 explains it in full.** Before any fix: v2 + small body + big postBuffer succeeded; v2 + 11 MB + default postBuffer failed; v0 behaved identically in both cases. Body size decides, not protocol version — git 2.55 does not use v2 for `receive-pack` and sends no `Git-Protocol` header on a push, so the wire is v0 either way.

## D5 — byte identity

**The bytes came back identical.** I recorded the push off the wire with a proxy, so this is the actual pack urgit decoded: 11,449,156 bytes, 1,373 objects, **637 `REF_DELTA`**, chains to **depth 6**. Three checks — whole object-set hash, a `git cat-file --batch` stream over exactly those 637 OIDs across three separate round trips (`99f0e575…e74071e6` every time), and the depth-6 336,494-byte blob compared directly. Plus `fsck --full` clean. Incidentally this is the first real exercise of the `%ref` branch of `resolve-pass`, which `QUESTIONS.md` §9 recorded as untested.

## Left undone

`OFS_DELTA` on the push side never ran (urgit does not advertise `ofs-delta`; changing that alters the wire contract, which the brief does not authorize). No `git` client walked the 401-reprobe loop with a real credential helper. No ceiling above 11.45 MB was probed. `git-github.hoon`'s outbound `receive-request` was read, not exercised. Wall times are single readings, not medians. All of this is in the report's "What I could not measure and why."

Cleanup: I stopped only the ship I started (PID 2311003) and the proxy (PID 2324700), by recorded PID. No `pkill`, `killall`, or `tmux kill-session`. `fakezod`, `fakenec`, and the three `t4-*` piers are all still running.
